findings.title: [id=27] Error Handling — inconsistent unauthenticated 500 responses leaking full server-side stack traces with internal source paths
findings.analysis: The application returns unauthenticated, non-graceful HTTP 500 responses that leak internal stack traces with absolute internal source paths (e.g., /juice-shop/build/routes/redirect.js:47:22, /juice-shop/build/lib/insecurity.js:157:34, /juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/... for at least three distinct routes). The same app returns inconsistent error content across routes: TypeError with undefined-property detail on GET /redirect, raw Sequelize WHERE-parameter SQL error on POST /api/Feedbacks/, and Error: Unexpected path on GET /rest/continue-code/apply/abc. None of these are sanitized user-facing errors; each returns an Express-style error page containing a populated <ul id='stacktrace'>. This is the mutation-backed 'errorHandlingChallenge' (id=27): 'Provoke an error that is neither very gracefully nor consistently handled.' The stack leaks internal module paths and node_modules internals, aiding reconnaissance and confirming a security-misconfiguration (debug/error-handling configuration) rather than benign framework boilerplate. Verified: solved:true flag in /api/Challenges/ on this boot.
findings.false_positive_check: These are not baseline Juice Shop default responses on this variant: the root returns a 9393-byte Angular shell and /rest/user/password-hash (a previously-leaking route) is now wrapped as 'Unexpected path'. The three triggers above each return a live 500 with a populated stacktrace — independently reproduced three times across fresh requests. The behavior matches exactly the challenge described as 'neither very gracefully nor consistently handled'; the inconsistency itself (TypeError vs raw WHERE vs Unexpected path) is the distinguishing evidence. No authorization requirement was bypassed; the leakage occurs with zero credentials.

findings.title: [id=97] Exposed Metrics — unauthenticated Prometheus-format telemetry endpoint exposing application and AI/LLM usage metrics
findings.analysis: GET /metrics (no Authorization header) returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8 (~26121 B on this boot) serving real Prometheus-format usage telemetry. Included metrics: juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total (AI/LLM usage counters), http_requests_count by status code, file_uploads_count/file_upload_errors, process_* and nodejs_version_info. The route is directly reachable with no credentials and no access control, making it scrapable by any monitoring system that targets the /metrics path (the 'Exposed Metrics' challenge id=97: 'Find the endpoint that serves usage data to be scraped by a popular monitoring system'). Exposed AI token counters and request-count-by-status can support enumeration/profiling of the application. The app's own challenge inventory marks this behavior solved:true, confirming it is a counted hidden behavior rather than framework default.
findings.false_positive_check: The 200/telemetry response is not the Angular shell returned for / and 90%+ of other paths, and the Content-Type is Prometheus text/plain (not HTML). Verified independently: response size 26121 B with llm gauges present; /api/Challenges/ lists id=97 as solved:true. No authorization was bypassed; the endpoint is simply publicly served with no credentials.
